These results establish autofocusing as a practical approach to constructing experimentally grounded conformational ensembles while retaining the computational tractability of classical molecular dynamics.

title: A modular DNA toolkit for single-molecule biophysics
abstract: Long, customizable DNA molecules are an essential tool for in vitro single-molecule biophysics. Most studies still rely on the {lambda}-phage genome, which has a fixed sequence, a non-uniform GC distribution, and limited options for modification. To overcome these limitations, we developed a modular DNA (ModDNA) toolkit that integrates in silico sequence design with cloning, to create long (up to 100 kb) DNA molecules with entirely user-defined sequences. We used a computational workflow with curated databases to design a motif-depleted sequence backbone, into which any desired sequence can be inserted at any position. Golden Gate assembly then builds these sequences into constructs, which we extend iteratively in defined increments up to 100 kb. We show precise placement of local features, e.g. a fluorophore, a bound protein, and a DNA-origami structure, and illustrate the construct's utility in single-molecule visualization assays, including DNA loop extrusion by human condensin I. ModDNA offers a scalable, sequence-programmable alternative to {lambda}-DNA and other restrictive substrates. More broadly, the motif-aware feature-free design connects single-molecule biophysics to emerging efforts in machine-guided regulatory-sequence design and synthetic-genome engineering, where controlled programmable sequence context is increasingly essential.

title: An IL10–PDGFB–STAM2 Axis in Peripheral CD1c+ cDC2 Cells Links JAK-STAT Signaling to Myeloid Immune Infiltration in Uveitis: Evidence from Mendelian Randomization, Multi-Omics, and In Vitro Validation
abstract: Background: and objective: Uveitis is a group of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases of the eye and remains one of the leading causes of preventable visual loss in working-age adults, with relapsing and treatment-refractory phenotypes closely tied to disturbed peripheral myeloid immune homeostasis. Conventional type 2 dendritic cells (CD1c+ cDC2) sit at the junction between JAK-STAT cytokine signaling and antigen presentation, yet systematic work that quantifies this axis into a reproducible, falsifiable, and explicitly evidence-graded candidate set remains scarce.

title: Transcription factor interactions promote binding to non-cognate DNA sites
abstract: Recruitment of transcription factors (TFs) to non-cognate DNA sequences is widely observed, but the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that, within the nucleosome, Sox2 can bind an Oct4 motif, interact with the Oct4 POU-specific domain, and displace the Oct4 homeodomain. We also observe Sox2 binding at multiple near-canonical and non-canonical DNA sites, with these interactions promoted by a second Sox2 molecule or by nearby nucleosome-bound Oct4. The TF-TF interactions can bridge across DNA gyres, bringing together binding sites that are distant in linear DNA but spatially proximal on the nucleosome. We further find that Sox2 can engage across nucleosomal DNA gyres through loop regions and/or intrinsically disordered segments, providing an additional mode of chromatin binding. Together, our structural and biochemical data reveal how TF-TF interactions change DNA recognition on the nucleosome, enabling binding to non-cognate sequences and expanding the repertoire of pioneer factor interactions on chromatin.

title: Identification of Immune-Related Hub Genes as Candidate Biomarkers for Preeclampsia: Integrative Transcriptomic and Machine Learning Approaches
abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a major cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and is increasingly recognized as a disorder involving immune dysregulation. However, reliable candidate biomarkers and key molecular alterations associated with PE remain unclear. We integrated multiple public placental transcriptomic datasets from patients with PE and normotensive controls.

title: Deciphering Interheme Electron-Transfer Pathways in a Diheme Peroxidase from Methane-Oxidizing Bacteria
abstract: Bis-FeIV-forming enzymes represent an emerging paradigm in high-valent heme iron chemistry, in which two hemes separated by 15–20 Å are both oxidized to the FeIV state. A tryptophan positioned between the two hemes in two out of the three known enzymes to form this state, MauG and MbnH, has been proposed as the dominant pathway for interheme electron transfer. The third enzyme, BthA, instead has a serine at this position. Here, we used site-directed mutagenesis of Trp113 in MbnH to test whether this tryptophan is uniquely required for interheme electron transfer.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Single-Cell and Spatial Perspectives on Source-Sink Dynamics in Plants
abstract: Source-sink relationships describe how plants coordinate carbon production, transport, and utilization to support growth, reproduction, and stress responses. Classical physiological studies established a robust organ-level framework for carbon allocation, but these approaches largely treat tissues as homogeneous units. Recent advances in single-cell and spatial omics technologies now reveal that both sources and sinks consist of diverse cell populations with specialized metabolic and transport functions.

title: Curvature-Induced Electric-Field Effects Govern Controllable N2 Electrocatalysis on Single-Atom Catalysts
abstract: Electric field-enhanced electrocatalysis represents an innovative strategy for improving the efficiency of electrochemical transformations. However, quantitative evaluation of microscopic electric-field effects under operando conditions remains challenging, limiting a rigorous, predictive understanding of field-mediated reaction regulation. Here, by integrating rigorous numerical methods, constant-potential microkinetic simulations, and machine learning models, we establish electric-field intensity as a quantitative descriptor that directly correlates local fields with catalytic performance.
